questions.question: When downshifting, what should you do?

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Can over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets affect riding ability?

options.text: Yes, they can affect a rider's ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
No, they usually won't affect riding ability.
No, they are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect a rider's ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can impact your riding ability. Check the side effects before taking any drug and riding.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about low-speed crashes?

options.text: They happen often, so they are not a concern.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: What clothing should a motorcycle rider wear?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
A jacket that covers your arms, but leave your legs exposed.
Pants that cover your legs, but leave your arms exposed.
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: What certification should a helmet have for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Downshifting causes the engine to slow the motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides good traction.

questions.question: When you ride an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride as you normally do, since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Be careful with a new bike. Get to know it before you start riding. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how they work.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be ridden in curves.
Should use the road shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. They do not handle curves the same way.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal checking routine.
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal checking routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before you change lanes, stop at an intersection, or slow down.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When it will be harder to stop than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it will be harder to stop than usual.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. This includes slippery roads, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and a driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. Your brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is okay to drag your feet.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet on the ground. Do not point your toes down because they might hit the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if you need to.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear proper ear protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Which types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps you stay safe in traffic.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, wear:
questions.explanation: Bright clothes help other drivers see you. Wear clothes that stand out during the day and at night.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem when the road is wet.
Makes it easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your skills.
Effects from alcohol may still exist.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Effects from alcohol may still exist.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. Even if you wait, alcohol can still hurt your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass if you can. Speeding up causes them to tailgate you at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.
